# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Status unchanged from last turn: display 0, light still YELLOW, wires 1 yellow, 2 blue, 3 red, 4 white, 5 green. Blind, I see your five-symbol gesture but I cannot decode it without a shared code. Mute, I see your gestures but we have no agreed meaning, so I will not act on a guess. Proposal: Mute, spell letters using the alphabet-list positions 1-26 = A-Z (symbol 1 = A, symbol 2 = B, ... symbol 26 = Z). Send one symbol per letter. I will read it and relay the instruction to Blind in speech, since I am the only channel from you to Blind.

Deaf has proposed a concrete code: gesture alphabet positions 1-26 = A-Z, one symbol per letter. That's decodable — Deaf can count the symbol's position in the list. This is the way to get the manual to me.

I should endorse Deaf's proposal to Mute, since I can speak to Mute and Mute can hear me. I'll confirm the scheme and urge Mute to spell the rule letter by letter.

Status: display 0, light YELLOW, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red 4 white 5 green. Still no rule. I must not cut.

Let me speak to Mute endorsing the A-Z spelling scheme, and gesture to Deaf to confirm I agree.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Agreed: Deaf's scheme is good. Mute, spell the manual's instruction letter by letter, one gesture symbol per letter, using the alphabet-list positions 1 to 26 for A to Z. Deaf will read it and speak the rule to me. I will not cut until I hear the rule in words. Status I have: display 0, light yellow, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red 4 white 5 green.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Code confirmed working. Mute's message decoded: COUNT GREEN AND YELLOW FLASHES. That is my job since I alone see the light. Light readings so far: turn1 green, turn2 yellow, turn3 yellow, turn4 green. Running tally: green = 2, yellow = 2. Current light is GREEN. Mute, I have the counts, send the next instruction for what to do with them. Blind, stand by to act on my relay.

Now the rule is emerging. Mute's instruction: "COUNT GREEN AND YELLOW FLASHES." Deaf's job — count flashes. Tally: green=2, yellow=2, current light green.

Wait, but the display reads 0. Hmm. The rule is to count green and yellow flashes. Then presumably a later instruction tells what to do with the count. Deaf is asking Mute for the next instruction.

So the flow: Mute gives rule in stages. Stage 1: count green and yellow flashes. Deaf counts. Stage 2 (pending): what to do with the counts.

I should stand by, but also keep the channel moving. I can speak to Mute to confirm I'm ready and ask for the next instruction. Gesture to Deaf to acknowledge.

Also note: display 0 — maybe display is irrelevant, or maybe the count relates to display. Deaf reports display 0 consistently.

Let me speak to Mute urging the next instruction, and gesture to Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Understood: rule is to count green and yellow flashes. Deaf's tally so far: green 2, yellow 2, current light green. I am ready to cut. Send the next instruction: what do the counts mean and which wire do I cut?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf here. Mute's message decoded: CUT WIRE TWO. This matches the rule: green flashes counted 2, and wire 2 is the target. Blind, your action: cut wire 2. It is the second wire; I cannot help you with its colour since you cannot see it, so identify it by position. My light tally: green = 2, yellow = 3. Mute, confirm wire two is correct and that counting is finished.

Deaf relayed: CUT WIRE TWO. Rule: green flashes counted 2 → wire 2. Deaf's tally green=2, yellow=3.

But wait — I should be careful. The rule was "count green and yellow flashes." Which count maps to the wire? Deaf says green=2 → wire 2. But why green and not yellow? Yellow=3 would give wire 3. Deaf asserts green count = 2 → wire 2. That's an assumption. Mute said "CUT WIRE TWO" explicitly, so the instruction is direct: cut wire 2. That's a direct decoded instruction, not an inference. Good.

However, I should double-check: is the count still changing? Light was green at turn 5, and Deaf says green=2, yellow=3 now — wait, at turn 4 green=2 yellow=2, current green. Now green=2 yellow=3? That means a yellow flash occurred. Hmm, the tally changed. If the count matters and it's still changing, cutting now might be premature.

Actually let me reconsider. Deaf's tally: turn1 green, turn2 yellow, turn3 yellow, turn4 green → green 2, yellow 2. Then turn5? Deaf said current green at turn 5 (that was turn 4's reading relayed). Now turn 6: green=2, yellow=3. So one more yellow appeared. The count is still moving.

But Mute's explicit instruction is "CUT WIRE TWO." Mute reads the manual and gives the instruction. I should trust the decoded instruction. But the changing tally is a concern — maybe the rule is "cut when green count equals wire number" or "cut the wire matching the count at the right moment."

Given Mute explicitly said CUT WIRE TWO, and Deaf confirms, I'll act. But let me be cautious: the instruction is clear and direct from the manual-holder. I'll cut wire 2.

Actually, I should act now — the bomb is armed and timing may matter. Mute gave the direct instruction. Cut wire 2.

Let me also speak/gesture to confirm. But the action is the priority.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```

I'll include a brief confirm message too.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Acting on your decoded instruction: cutting wire 2 now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
